title: Specify what the committed-schema generator stamp holds (OPAG-354 item 3 mechanism)
description:
OPAG-354 item 3 delegates the MECHANISM to this repository: "What exactly the stamp holds is NOT decided here and is lore-cli's to specify with measurement, because lore-cli raised the one open objection and holds the generator." Read from opum-ai/opum-agent's committed .quest/tasks/OPAG-354.json at ref main, not from the routing message. The architectural commitment is fixed and not reopened here: committed schemas must carry enough generator provenance for the tool to distinguish "type removed from profile" (prune correct) from "binary older than the tree" (prune destroys unreleased work), and drift must gain a third outcome rather than collapsing cannot-judge into a destructive remedy.

THE OPEN TENSION AS OPAG-354 STATES IT: a per-release version stamp may churn every schema file on every release; a profile digest says the artifact came from a different profile but not in WHICH DIRECTION, while a version says direction and is the thing this fleet elsewhere refuses to trust for capability detection.

THE CHURN HALF IS NOW MEASURED, and it settles against the version stamp. Against this repository's own tags, reading the tree SHA of .lore/schemas at each:

  v0.6.0  4bb5609ac74d76c1e51dac90959de4c1f323a549  7 files
  v0.6.1  4bb5609ac74d76c1e51dac90959de4c1f323a549  7 files
  v0.6.2  4bb5609ac74d76c1e51dac90959de4c1f323a549  7 files
  v0.7.0  4bb5609ac74d76c1e51dac90959de4c1f323a549  7 files
  v0.8.0  125934b1dab5ea0fe15a5c154b7f7269724bcbbf  7 files
  dev     700f1ed407cde2bce68137ac5362b69dfb2a4a35  8 files  (Arc, LCLI-554)

Byte-identical across four consecutive releases, and only 3 commits have ever touched .lore/schemas/. So a per-release version stamp would have rewritten all 7 files at v0.6.1, v0.6.2 and v0.7.0 while nothing about the profile changed -- 21 file rewrites carrying no information, in a directory that genuinely changes about twice in five releases. The churn objection was real and is now quantified rather than asserted. A profile digest changes when the profile changes: 2 of 5 here, which is not churn, it is signal.

THE DIRECTION HALF DISSOLVES RATHER THAN BEING TRADED OFF, and this is the substantive proposal. Direction is not required for the safety property. The destructive action is PRUNE specifically, and prune is safe only when the tool can affirm the committed artifact came from a profile it actually owns. A digest answers exactly that question: digest matches a profile I generate -> I own this, prune is a real finding; digest does not match -> I cannot judge this from here, third outcome, never a prune. The tool never needs to know whether it is older or newer to AVOID the destructive act -- it only needs to know whether the artifact is its own. Direction is needed to WORD the message well, not to decide the action, which is why the fleet's refusal to trust version comparisons for capability detection does not bite here.

PROPOSED SPECIFICATION, for review rather than as a settled answer:
- key the DECISION on a profile digest, carried in each committed schema
- carry the generating lore version ALONGSIDE it, used only for the human-readable message ("generated by lore X, this is lore Y"), never as the predicate
- unknown digest => cannot-be-checked-from-here, exit distinguishable from both clean and drifted, and never a prune suggestion

This mirrors LCLI-548's verified/failed/cannot-be-checked-from-here exactly, which is why OPAG-354 cites it. Note the two existing errors are NOT equally dangerous and the fix must preserve that: "no longer matches what this profile generates" rewrites a file (recoverable from git); "no type owns this schema -- prune it" deletes one.

NOT A SUBSTITUTE FOR LCLI-545, per OPAG-354 item 4: 545 improves the wording of advice that is still undecidable underneath. Neither closes the other. OPAG-353 remains the fleet operating rule for binaries already on disk that will never receive this fix.

A cross-fleet consequence to state rather than discover: all 71 committed schema files across the ten repositories share one identical top-level key set and none carries provenance (measured by opum-agent on OPAG-354). So whatever shape this takes, every repository's committed schemas become stale on the release that introduces it, and the rollout needs to not look like the 0.8.0 event in LCLI-545.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The stamp's contents are specified and the version-vs-digest tension is resolved with the measurement that settles it, not restated as an open question
lore schema export writes the stamp, and lore check keys its prune/no-prune decision on it rather than on type ownership alone
A committed schema whose stamp the running binary does not recognise produces a third outcome distinguishable in the exit code from both clean and drifted, and NEVER suggests pruning
The rewrite case and the delete case stay distinguishable in both message and exit code, preserving the asymmetry OPAG-354 item 5 names
The churn cost is re-measured against this repo's tags after the change and stated, so the objection is closed with a number rather than a judgement
A rollout note exists for the release that introduces it, since all 71 committed schemas fleet-wide go stale at once -- LCLI-545 records what that felt like at 0.8.0

implementationNotes: WHY THE TOOL-SIDE FIX MATTERS MOST HERE, measured 2026-09-20 after opum-cli-e2e proposed a structural shortcut for OPAG-353. Their check: if a repo's .lore/profile.toml is entirely commented out, the bundle uses lore's built-in types, so an older binary's export has nothing to prune and the destructive direction is unreachable -- greppable, falsified only by someone uncommenting the file. IT INVERTS HERE. This repository has NO .lore/profile.toml at all (.lore/ holds agents, cache, config.toml, schemas), yet arc.schema.json is committed. The type vocabulary lives in src/core/profile.ts:1074 (name: "Arc"). lore-cli does not CONFIGURE a profile, it IS the profile. So a file-based check reads absent-file as empty-therefore-safe, which is exactly backwards, and the fleet sweep would score this repo as safe. THE PREDICATE WANTS RESTATING, not the grep: 'can this repository's effective profile differ from the installed binary's?' For a consumer that reduces to their greppable check. For a generator it is PERMANENTLY TRUE, because the effective profile is source under development and dev is ahead of every released binary by construction -- there is no safe window except immediately after a release, before the next profile change lands. CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS TASK: OPAG-353's operating rule can help the nine consumer repositories and cannot help this one, because the unsafe condition here is structural rather than occasional. The stamp is the only remedy that reaches lore-cli's own bundle, which raises this task's priority relative to how it was filed. Reported to opum-cli-e2e so opum-agent gets the predicate rather than the grep before measuring the fleet.
